about: Games Flato3D has been made to work with: what to install, the OGL3D.ini values that differ from the template, and the state of each. The installer will apply these as profiles. Candidates not yet worked on are in game_candidates.json. 'test' holds the steps for tools\analysis\gametest.ps1.

games.name: Technobabylon
notes: Rule feet: sprites stand at the depth of their bottom edge, rooms slope back towards the top of the screen.
Scissor batches: 0 = room, 1 = overlays/GUI, 2 = cursor (screen_batch 1 keeps the GUI at the screen).

games.name: Huntdown
games.api: Direct3D 11 (-force-glcore not built into the player)
notes: WineD3D's d3d11/dxgi must be the renamed copies (w3d11.dll, wxgi.dll): the NVIDIA OpenGL driver presents through the system D3D11 and would pick up a module called d3d11.dll.
WineD3D CSMT must stay on (Unity creates resources from other threads); no csmt registry key.
The game turns vsync off; swap_interval = 1 forces it on, otherwise a tear line runs across the woven picture.
Unity draws each parallax plane as its own draw call, often from one atlas: group = draw (every draw is a layer), order_curve = 0.5 gives the background planes more of the depth range.
The sprite atlas sits on texture unit 1 (unit 0 holds a 0x0 placeholder); only the units a program samples count, because WineD3D leaves earlier render targets bound on others.
The scene buffer is a texture view (render target view) and the final pass reads another view of the same texture; the composition order follows views.
known_issues: Measured on a cutscene only (layers -44..-96 px with the old depth_screen 1.05); gameplay depth to be confirmed by the user.

test.reaches: street cutscene of the first mission, then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Saves are backed up in test-backups\Huntdown (only Unity session counters change).

games.name: Door Kickers: Action Squad
notes: The loader (version.dll) is required: Steam's overlay maps the system d3d9 early and the exe has no GetProcAddress import.
WineD3D CSMT off (registry key): with it on, the title -> menu step deadlocked under the NVIDIA DXGI-layered present.
The level is drawn at about 416x234 into a 1024x1024 cache (left half colour, right half normals), then scaled to the screen: the cache is made stereo (layer cache), cache_scale = 416/1024.
F5 toggles the game's frame statistics; our hotkeys are kept from the game ([Keys] swallow = 1).
separation and depth_screen are the user's own settings.
Only a target drawn into in the same frame becomes a layer cache (WineD3D also attaches atlases to its own framebuffers for uploads).
known_issues: Depth inside the low-resolution cache moves in cache pixels (about 9 screen px per step): only a few depth levels. Planned: render the cache larger.

Now and then (seen in automated launches of DK and Huntdown, mostly the first one after replacing the DLLs) the game stops after frame 3 for about 100 s, the render thread waiting inside the NVIDIA driver under WineD3D. Not shader compilation (the program links in 43 ms on a cold cache). Cause unknown.

test.reaches: gameplay, then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Mouse clicks work (3840x2160 screen pixels), keyboard input is unreliable.

games.name: FRAMED Collection (FRAMED, FRAMED 2)
notes: screen_batch = 0: the game sets glScissor before many draws, so the AGS rule (later scissor batches are UI) would put the whole picture at the screen.
Each comic panel is drawn as frame + picture; repeated runs of the same draws share a depth, so the panels sit side by side on one plane.
Measured on the first puzzle of FRAMED: blinds +56 px, room +36..42 px, panels -2 px, hint arrow -28 px (separation 25).

The panel pictures are videos (YUV in texture1/uTexture/vTexture of program c05a6bab), so the figures arrive inside one picture. [Flat] silhouette rewrites that fragment shader: dark pixels (the black silhouettes) are sampled through a per-eye shifted coordinate and stand in front of the picture.
Silhouette check (first puzzle, separation 8.4% at the time): figures +4.8 px nearer than the panel picture (half-resolution dump), exactly the configured shift.
known_issues: Only the first puzzle of FRAMED measured; FRAMED 2 not yet tried.
A panel's picture sits slightly in front of its own frame (drawn after it).
Silhouettes come forward as flat cutouts; white details inside a figure (glasses, flowers) stay at the picture's depth, and a thin strip of background is repeated where a figure moved away.
Remote SBS check: the user preferred separation about 3% with depth_screen 1.2 (not saved).

test.reaches: first puzzle of FRAMED (collection menu -> FRAMED -> title), then Ctrl+F12 dump

games.name: Astral Ascent
install: loader/x64/version.dll (2026-10-15 or later: patches static imports)
remove: d3d11.dll, dxgi.dll, nvapi64.dll of a geo-11 install (they would load instead of WineD3D)
games.verified_by_user: 2026-10-18 (NVIDIA GPU; on an Intel GPU the sky differed between the eyes, report 2026-10-17)
notes: No upscale: the game makes itself DPI aware at run time (SDL) and has no resolution or fullscreen option, so it always renders at the desktop resolution (4K) and upscale changes nothing (checked 2026-10-19). Its own scale option makes the UI larger. The 1600x900 limit on PCGamingWiki does not hold.
The exe binds d3d11.dll before any of our code runs; the loader points that import at w3d11.dll (the system d3d11 stays for the GPU driver).
Every object is one quad with its own texture, drawn in layer order: drawing order gives the layers.
Text is drawn glyph by glyph into a scratch target that is cleared and composited several times a frame: each use is one layer, so lines are flat.
Animated sprites change texture every few frames: groups new to the last frame's layout take the place after the group drawn before them.
Measured in the first area (separation 25): sky +28..54 px, islands +30, swords/ruins +20..26, pillars and ground +8, player -6, HUD -14..-18.

Played through the hub areas (ruins, altar, garden, cliff) with movement, jumps and attacks: no hangs or errors, 60 fps, one A-B-A flicker that was a game effect in both eyes. Garden: sky +40..64 px, ground +28, trees +20, characters 0..-6, pergola -12, low clouds -14, HUD -20. Cliff: far islands +40..64, rock island +28, characters 0, big foreground cliff -18.
known_issues: Intel GPU (another PC, report 2026-10-17): the background sky differs between the eyes. NVIDIA works; only NVIDIA GPUs are supported.
Characters stand in front of the ground they walk on (the ground is drawn before them, so drawing order puts it farther): up to about 30 px in the garden.
Dialogue scenes: portrait, box and text are one flat UI layer in front of the scene.

test.reaches: first area after the opening dialogue (intro skipped, save slot 1 loaded), then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Loads and advances save slot 1: back up Saved Games\Astral Ascent\<steamid> first and restore it afterwards.

games.name: Machinarium
games.engine: Amanita Design's own engine (2020 release; Machinarium_old_32bit_DX9.exe is the old Flash version)
games.api: Direct3D 12 by default; OpenGL with the -ogl switch
games.verified_by_user: 2026-10-18 (play, SR weaving; status report works, separation 38.33 saved with Ctrl+F7)
notes: The exe imports d3d12.dll and opengl32.dll; it draws with Direct3D 12 unless started with -ogl. Steam does not pass it, so OGL3D appends it ([Inject] add_args = -ogl, GetCommandLine redirected before the game reads it).

With -ogl it draws fixed-function OpenGL (no shaders): orthographic sprites into one 3840x2160 framebuffer, copied to the window. The fixed-function path offsets the projection per draw; layers follow the drawing order (18-23 texture groups in the first scenes: far scrap heap, middle, props, foreground, the inventory bar in front).
It clears only the stencil buffer between masked pieces (glClear(GL_STENCIL_BUFFER_BIT)); those clears do not start a new picture, or the scene collapsed into 2-3 layers.
Renders at the native 4K: no upscale (PCGamingWiki's 'no 4K' is about the old Flash version).
Steam asks how to start it (Machinarium / Play with DirectX 9 / Play with DirectX 12): choose the first entry. The other two were not tried.

Scenes are drawn as Flash shapes with bitmap fills; pieces of the background picture are drawn again later (walk-behinds). User report 2026-10-18 (tower scene): such a piece stood out as a rectangle. A fixed-function draw that maps the same texture onto the screen exactly as an earlier picture now joins that picture's layer, unless it covers something drawn on the picture since (the ground edge over the robot's feet stays in front).

Rule feet since 2026-10-18 (fixed-function feet rule, OGL3D-SR flato3d): the scene picture is the floor sloping back (+60 top .. -26 bottom px at separation 25), walk-behinds keep its slope, the robot's parts (shadow, legs, body, head: two textures) stand together at its feet (-2 px on its ledge), a thought bubble drawn over the robot is no farther than it, the inventory bar and its icons stay at the screen. Under the order rule the robot stood ~50 px in front of the ground it walks on.
known_issues: Checked with dumps in the first scenes and the tower scene only; not played through yet.
Feet rule: tall pieces of the scene picture lean back with the floor slope (the towers); big foreground pieces reaching the screen bottom sit at sprite_min (-24 px) up to their top.

test.reaches: clicks through the intro screens, then the menu's Continue (game coordinates 1000,705; New game is at 1120,472 and overwrites the saved progress - do not click it once the user has played), then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Steam's launch chooser needs a click: for automated runs put a temporary steam_appid.txt (40700) next to the exe, start the exe itself, and delete the file afterwards. Saves: Steam Cloud, <Steam>\userdata\<account>\40700\remote\Machinarium.dat (7 slots and the settings; the Amanita-Design.Machinarium folders in %APPDATA% / %LOCALAPPDATA% stay empty) - back it up before play tests. Set output = sbs for automated checks.

games.name: Rocketbirds: Hardboiled Chicken
games.engine: PSSG (NVIDIA Cg runtime, shaders compiled with the arbvp1/arbfp1 assembly profiles)
games.api: OpenGL (ARB assembly vertex/fragment programs, no GLSL)
notes: Installed on the OpenGL route the game stayed flat: 'shaders injected 0' - the PSSG engine calls cgCreateProgram with arbvp1/arbfp1, so its draws run ARB assembly programs. The wrapper now rewrites ARB vertex programs (offset from program.env[255]) and reads the texture units of ARB fragment programs.

The window is created with 4x multisampling. GL refuses blits into a multisampled back buffer, so with output = sbs / tab / left / right the composed eyes never reached the screen: the game's own picture stayed, separation changes showed nothing (user report 2026-10-21; Ctrl+F12 dumps looked right because they read the eye buffers). Fixed in the wrapper: on a multisampled window the eyes are drawn in as textured quads (log: "output drawn into the window"). SR weaving was not affected. Checked on screen: menu +30..35 px, text -6 px at separation 25; +44..51 / -9 at 36.7.
Forcing Cg to GLSL ([Inject] cg_glsl = 1) turned the screen white: the engine passes its own profile and assembly-only options (-profileopts MaxLocalParams=256). Keep cg_glsl = 0.
screen_batch = 0: the game sets a viewport/scissor before every pass, so later batches are not UI.
Measured (separation 17.9 set in game): chapter 1 title 'Sito in the Jungle' foreground tree silhouette near, jungle and poster wall behind; first gameplay (unloading area) -28..+44 px, median +24.
known_issues: Depth per draw only (an ARB vertex program has no geometry shader for a per-sprite spread inside one draw).
Starts with a 'connect an Xbox 360 controller' prompt (Enter continues).

test.reaches: controller prompt -> chapter 1 title -> first gameplay (unloading area), then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Saves are in the game folder's Save\ (P0-LEVEL, PROFILES, SETTINGS): back up to test-backups\Rocketbirds\Save and restore after tests. Set output = sbs before automated checks (the user watches remotely).

games.name: Samorost 2
games.engine: Adobe AIR captive runtime (Flash content drawn with Stage3D; some objects through filter buffers)
games.verified_by_user: 2026-10-18 (play, SR weaving; seams gone; the user saved separation 32.9 and depth_screen 0.75 with Ctrl+F7)
notes: Installed by the installer on the WineD3D Direct3D 11 route (renamed set + loader), feet rule from the candidate list, upscale on (no 4K).

With upscale the game first showed 'not responding' and ignored clicks: the presentation window was made on WineD3D's render thread. Fixed in the wrapper (the window is made on the game window's thread).

Scene pictures are split into pieces (a tentacle is drawn as an upper and a lower piece; the spaceship as several). Under the feet rule each narrow piece stood at its own bottom edge, so a horizontal line and rectangles showed where pieces meet (user report). New key plane_tall = 0.12: a piece at least 1/16 of the screen high follows the floor slope whatever its width (plane_size/plane_height need wide AND high), so the pieces line up; the bottom strip of the ground (wide, low pieces) too. Small sprites (characters, crates) still stand at their bottom edge. The order rule was tried and was worse (pieces in different layers).

With depth_screen 0.75 the floor came nearer than sprite_min (-0.25) allowed sprites, so pieces at the bottom stepped back (a horizontal line near the bottom). sprite_min now moves with depth_screen (unchanged at depth_screen 0).
Measured (tentacle scene, the user's separation 32.9 / depth_screen 0.75): one slope from +30 (top) to -90 px (bottom) without steps.
known_issues: Objects drawn through filter buffers (some seed heads on the tentacles) come out near the screen (+2 px) in front of their stems (+30..40): their depth is worked out in the small buffer, not on the screen.
Tall objects lean back with the floor slope instead of standing upright (the price of no seams).

test.reaches: title -> first scene (the spaceship on the hill), then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Steam app 40720 (steam://rungameid/40720). Saves: %APPDATA%\amanitadesign.samorost3\Local Store (s2save.bin, init.dat) - back up before play tests. Set output = sbs for automated checks; OGL3D reloads OGL3D.ini while the game runs.

games.name: Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley
games.engine: Unity (URP, IL2CPP), a 3D scene with a perspective camera
notes: By the 2026-10-18 decision (Flato3D does flat 2D only) a real 3D game belongs to Geo Gaming Hub (geo-11 on the game's own Direct3D 11); the user installed it with Flato3D, so this profile stays.

Not a flat 2D game: the scene is real 3D seen through a perspective camera. With flat depth on, auto convergence stays off and convergence stays at its start value 3 while the scene lies 60-85 units away, so everything sat at the far limit (+46..48 px of 48), as flat as a picture. Flat depth off: auto convergence settles at about 65; on the title the sky is at +39 px, the hills +10..31, Snufkin and the foreground -9..+3, the menu at the screen. In play the ground slopes from +11 px (top) to +1 px (bottom), trees in front at -8 px, speech bubbles at the screen.

The right eye lacked the landscape (log: 'fbo 14: right-eye copy incomplete (0x8cd7)'): WineD3D renders into multisample textures made with glTexStorage2DMultisample and attaches texture views of them; the wrapper made the right copy with mutable storage, which cannot have views. Fixed in the wrapper (2026-10-20): glTexStorage2DMultisample is tracked and the copy is immutable like the original.
known_issues: Checked with automated dumps only (title and the first meadow); not yet played with SR weaving.

test.reaches: title menu -> Continue -> the meadow (Snufkin with a speech bubble), then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Continue loads the last save: back up %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Hyper Games\Snufkin - Melody of Moominvalley first (test-backups\Snufkin) and restore it afterwards. Continue sits at (660,960) on a 3840x2160 screen with output = sbs.

games.name: Blade Assault
notes: Colours: Unity's post-processing renders its colour grading lookup table (a 1024x32 strip) every frame. The wrapper took it for a layer cache (a target drawn into the stereo scene), made it stereo and shifted it in the right eye, which turned the right eye bright red on the title. Fixed in the wrapper (2026-10-20): a strip (one side more than 4x the other) is never a layer cache.

Depth: Unity's 2D lights draw every lit sprite reading the screen's light texture (a stereo target), and such draws counted as composite passes, at the screen: the whole scene came out flat (both eyes identical). Fixed in the wrapper (2026-10-20): a draw that reads a stereo target and also draws an ordinary picture of its own (64 px or more, not a strip) is a lit sprite and gets its order depth; one that redraws a layer drawn before keeps that layer's depth; a primitive over the whole screen still stays at the screen (post-processing).
screen_batch = 0: WineD3D sets the viewport and scissor between the light passes, so the scene is drawn in batches 5 to 29 and the AGS rule (later batches are UI) kept it all at the screen.
Measured in the first corridor (opening dialogue open): the corridor at +12 px, parts in front of it at +6 px, the dialogue box in front of the scene.
known_issues: Measured during the opening dialogue only; the depth in play is to be confirmed by the user.
Some starts take over a minute (the NEOWIZ logo stays up); automated runs wait 80 s.

test.reaches: title -> Start -> the first corridor with the opening dialogue, then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Saves: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\TeamSuneat\BladeAssault (test-backups\BladeAssault) - back up before play tests. Clicks do not select the title menu; Enter does.

games.name: The Messenger
notes: Hang: the game stopped responding after seconds to minutes (also without the wrapper and without SR). WineD3D wakes its command stream thread with thread alerts (NtAlertThreadByThreadId); an alert left pending after a timed wait breaks the thread's next critical-section wait on Windows 11 24H2+, and ntdll loops in RtlpWaitOnCriticalSection forever. Fixed in the wrapper (2026-10-24): WineD3D's GetProcAddress gets no thread-alert functions, so it wakes the thread with an event. Before: 11 hangs in 19 runs; after: 10 sbs and 5 SR runs of 120 s with no hang. Details in tools/hang/README.md.
CSMT must stay on: csmt=0 crashes at start (Unity uses D3D11 from several threads, as in Huntdown). -force-glcore does not work (no OpenGL renderer in this build).

Measured with the installer's Unity defaults (order, one layer per draw), separation 25, dumps 1920x1080 per eye: title - stars, moon and mountains +68 px, logo +24 px, menu -10..-14 px, credits -20..-28 px; first scene (Ninja Village, opening dialogue) - sunset sky +52 px, middle trees and cliffs +38 px, top foliage +24 px, ledge +4..6 px, the ninja -6 px, dialogue box -26..-28 px.
known_issues: Measured on the title and the opening dialogue only; the depth in play is to be confirmed by the user.
The ninja stands about 10 px in front of the ledge under it (-6 px against +4 px).

test.reaches: intro story and "press any button" skipped with Enter -> menu Start (Space) -> save slot 1 (Space) -> Ninja Village with the opening dialogue, then Ctrl+F12 dump
test.notes: Saves: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Sabotage Studio\The Messenger\SaveGame.txt (test-backups\TheMessenger) - back up before play tests. The menu and the save slots ignore Enter; Space selects. On the save slot screen holding left Ctrl deletes the save: never press Ctrl+F12 there. The intro story runs about 60 s. For hang tests: tools\hang\hang_loop.ps1 -AppId 764790 -Proc TheMessenger.

games.name: Home
games.engine: GameMaker Studio 2 runner (2026 update v1.7.1; side-view pixel horror adventure)
notes: The candidate list had it as GameMaker: Studio 1, Direct3D 9, x86 (the 2017 build). The current Steam build (v1.7.1, 2026) is the GameMaker Studio 2 runner, x64, Direct3D 11 (data.win GEN8 version 2). The exe imports d3d11.dll statically; the loader points that import at w3d11.dll. The installer took the WineD3D Direct3D 11 route from its own detection.
The game runs at 30 fps by design (game speed 30 in data.win): 'frame 600' every 20 s in OGL3D.log is normal.

Each room is one draw of tall pieces (wallpaper strips, wainscot, side walls) that reach below the bottom of the screen. Under the feet rule each narrow piece stood at its own bottom edge, below the screen, so the whole room came out at -14 px, in front of the character (-10 px) who stands in front of it. plane_tall = 1 (half the screen height) makes those pieces follow the floor slope. The character (about 0.7 of the screen height) and the windows still stand at their bottom edge; door frames are about at the threshold.

The order rule was tried too: the wall is flat (+38 px) and the character at +10 px, but a dialogue card draws all its glyphs in one draw, and the order rule spreads one draw over its depth slot, so a line of text would slant by about 8 px. Kept feet.

Measured with feet + plane_tall 1 (separation 25, dumps 1920x1080 per eye): title - logo +10 px, buttons -2..-6 px, version text -12 px. First room - wall +16 (top) .. 0 px (chair rail), windows +2 px (on the sill, flush with the wall there), wainscot -4..-8 px, the character -10 px, the flashlight vignette (a full-screen darkness overlay) +34 (top) .. +4 px (bottom). Second room - wall +26 .. 0 px, potted plant, door frame and character -10 px. No blocks differ between the eyes; the flicker probe found nothing while walking.
known_issues: Dialogue cards are wider than plane_size, so they lean back with the floor slope (+26 top .. -6 bottom px); their text lines sit on the card's surface (+20, +12 px).
Pieces taller than half the screen lean back instead of standing upright. A character drawn that tall would lean too (not seen).
The flashlight vignette is one sloping plane: where it darkens the bottom of the scene it is a little behind what it covers (+4 px over -6..-10 px).

games.name: Axiom Verge
games.api: OpenGL through FNA3D (its Windows default is Direct3D 11)
notes: FNA3D picks Direct3D 11 on Windows, and the wrapper never loads: set the Steam launch option /gldevice:OpenGL (FNA's own switch; Axiom Verge also takes -opengl). The environment variable FNA3D_FORCE_DRIVER=OpenGL works too, but Steam restarts the game through itself (SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary) and drops it. OGL3D's add_args cannot help: opengl32.dll is only loaded after FNA3D has chosen its driver.

The Flato3D loader (version.dll) never loads in these .NET games: the runtime has System32's version.dll mapped before SDL2.dll imports it. FNA draws with OpenGL itself, so only opengl32.dll is needed.

Black screen until the wrapper fix of 2026-10-28: FNA's shaders come from MojoShader and write gl_FrontColor and gl_TexCoord[n] through macros (#define vs_oT0 gl_TexCoord[0]); the flat-depth geometry shader looked for built-ins only outside preprocessor lines and passed none of them on. The bodies of the macros a shader uses now count.

FNA renders every render target through one framebuffer object and swaps its colour attachment. The wrapper told targets apart by framebuffer number: viewport changes between targets started new scissor batches (screen_batch 1 put the whole scene at the screen: disparity 0), and the composition order took all targets for one scratch target (the scene collapsed into one layer). Batches and the composition order now count a framebuffer with its colour attachment as the target (2026-10-28).

The game draws at 480x270 and scales up: depth comes in steps of 4 px (one game pixel on a 1920-wide eye). The HUD and the dialogue box are drawn into a target of their own, one layer per 8x8 texture, so with the even order curve the 8 world layers bunched into the far fifth (+24..28 px); order_curve 0.4 spreads them.
upscale = 1: the wrapper makes the game DPI aware, and it then opened a 1920x1080 window on the 4K desktop; with upscale it fills the screen (presentation window 3840x2160).

Measured (separation 25, px on a 1920-wide eye): title (order_curve 1) - far tiles +32, near tiles +24, logo +8, menu -8. First room (order_curve 0.4) - Trace +16, the terrain walls drawn after him +8, dialogue box and portrait 0. 60 fps.

games.name: Blasphemous 2
games.engine: Unity 2021, IL2CPP (pixel side-scroller; the world is drawn into several 640x360 targets and scaled up)
notes: Tested 2026-10-29 on the MiniPC: AMD Radeon RX 7600M XT, not NVIDIA. Installer defaults for Unity, output sbs, game version 3.0.0. Runs at 60 fps; about 5 minutes on the title, the menus and in play with no hang; 82 shaders injected, none failed.
Unlike Blasphemous it fills the whole 3840x2160 window (no black bars).

Frame structure (Ctrl+F12 trace): the world is drawn into several 640x360 targets that are combined and scaled up, then the HUD. Each target counts its own drawing order. Depth steps are coarse (12 px at separation 25).

Measured with separation 25, dumps 1920x1080 per eye: title - logo -12 px, 'press any button' -26..-28 px, copyright lines -18..-22 px (the whole title stands in front of the screen). Play (the prie-dieu of the save and the rooms on both sides): far rock pillars and statues +24..+36 px, floor and platforms +24..+36 px, the prie-dieu and cherubs +12 px, the Penitent One 0 px, fog in the foreground -24..-30 px, HUD -16..-18 px, tears counter -10..-14 px.

order_weight 0.02 with order_curve 1 (2026-10-29): between the floor (draw 18) and the Penitent One (draw 28) Unity draws nine small sprites (the prie-dieu, cherubs, lights); with one step each he stood 24..36 px in front of the floor. Now the gap is 12 px (one 640x360 pixel): prie-dieu room floor +12, the Penitent One 0, far rocks +24..+36; dark room floor 0, him -12; blood rain platform +24, him +12, vines +60. Title and menus 0..-28 px.
Confirmed by the user on 2026-10-29 with order_weight 0.02: works well.

Video cutscenes (Helios3D, NVIDIA, 10-29): the right eye was pink. The cutscene video is converted from Y, U and V planes the game uploads from the CPU every frame (1920x1080 and 960x540, window-shaped, so they had right-eye copies); the copies were not kept up to date, and Y near 0 with U and V high gives pink. Found with trace_steps saving both eyes: the first pass reading the planes was the first to differ. The wrapper now treats a texture the game uploads from the CPU as a picture: no right-eye copy, and the framebuffers it is attached to stay mono. The video is flat (one picture, +68 px), subtitles -24 px. Eight small window-shaped sprite textures lost their copies the same way at start; Astral Ascent, which also has some, measured the same in an A/B.

Vertical hairlines in the backgrounds (user report, Helios3D, 10-30): 1-2 px vertical lines through the cloud layer and the background below the bridge, cut off by the sprites in front (the Penitent One, the bridge) - layer seams. The world is drawn at 640x360 and scaled up, so a per-eye shift of a fraction of a target pixel lands tile edges between texels (the neighbouring texel bleeds through) and rounds adjacent tiles differently (a gap), as Axiom Verge's sway. snap_pixels = 1 rounds each eye's shift to whole target pixels; the depth steps are then one target pixel (12 px at 4K), so a lowered separation (the user's ini had 7.04) wants raising again. Applied to the user's ini on 10-30; the user confirmed on the panel the same day that the lines are gone.
